statement: Simplify $\dfrac{\sqrt{3}+\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{3}-\sqrt{2}}$ and hence write it in the form $a+b\sqrt{6}$ where $a$ and $b$ are integers.
solution:
Multiply numerator and denominator by $\sqrt{3}+\sqrt{2}$:
$$\frac{(\sqrt{3}+\sqrt{2})^{2}}{(\sqrt{3})^{2}-(\sqrt{2})^{2}}=\frac{3+2+2\sqrt{6}}{3-2}=5+2\sqrt{6}.$$
Thus $a=5$ and $b=2$.
hints: Multiply top and bottom by the conjugate of the denominator.
